newsitem.title: UK: Panel says Lithuania nuclear plant unsafe - EBRD.
newsitem.headline: Panel says Lithuania nuclear plant unsafe - EBRD.

text.p: An independent panel of safety experts has recommended that Lithuania shut down its Ignalina nuclear power plant until it can be made safer, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said on Friday.
The plant's two reactors are due to be closed for maintenance this year.

"Neither of the two units...should be restarted after the planned 1997 shutdown for maintenance until important safety issues in design and operation are resolved," the Bank quoted the panel as saying.
The panel was commissioned by the EBRD and the Lithuanian government on behalf of the Nuclear Safety Account, a multilateral fund.
The plant, which supplies most of the Baltic state's electricity needs, was temporarily closed last August after a leak was detected in the cooling system.
Its reactors are the largest of the infamous Chernobyl-style RBMK models operating in the former Soviet Union.
